paper.title: Efficient Automatic CASH via Rising Bandits

unmapped: Rested rising bandit: arm k's reward on its n-th pull is a deterministic fixed function r_k(n) in [0,1], increasing and concave in n (Assumption 1)
Objective is the maximum observed reward max_t r_{pi(t)}(N+1) within T, regret against the best pull sequence (not cumulative reward)
Environment is deterministic with rewards depending on the learner's own pull counts; mapped to adversarial_adaptive only as closest vocabulary
settings.definition_quote: each arm $k$ has a fixed underlying reward function denoted by $r_k(.)$. All the reward functions are bounded within $[0, 1]$. When the agent pulls arm $k$ for the $n^{th}$ time, he receives an instantaneous reward $r_k(n)$. ... the objective of the agent in CASH is to maximize the observed reward within $T$ ... $J(T;\pi) = \max_{t=1:T} r_{\pi(t)}(N_{\pi(t)}(t) + 1)$ ... $R(T;\pi) = \max_{\tilde{\pi} \in \Pi}\{J(T;\tilde{\pi})\} - J(T; \pi)$. Assumption 1 (Rising) $\forall k$, $r_k(n)$ is bounded, increasing, and concave in $n$.

algorithms.name: Online algorithm for Rising Bandit (elimination with concave upper bounds)

symbols.r_star: reward function r_{k*}(.) of the optimal arm for horizon T
symbols.gamma_id: gamma(T) = max_k gamma_k(T), the number of steps needed to distinguish sub-optimal arm k from the optimal arm via the elimination bounds
symbols.n_paper: the paper's n in the bound (undefined in the statement; likely the number of arms K)

conditions: Assumption 1: each r_k(n) bounded, increasing and concave in n

source.quote: Suppose Assumption 1 holds. The proposed algorithm achieves regret bounded by, R(T; \bar{\pi}) \le r_{k_{\ast}^T}(T) - r_{k_{\ast}^T}(T - (n-1)\gamma(T)).

results.notes: Regret is on the maximum-observed-reward objective, not cumulative; quantity 'other'. Rewards are deterministic so the bound holds surely. The symbol n in the statement is not defined; probably K.

symbols.r_star: reward function of the optimal arm

source.quote: When the problem-dependent term $\gamma(T)$ satisfies: $\gamma(T) \le \frac{KT - T}{K(K-1)}$, the regret of the proposed algorithm will not be worse than the average strategy's. R(T; \bar{\pi}) \le R(T; \pi_{uni}).

results.notes: Comparison with uniform allocation policy; expression substitutes the paper's formula for R(T; pi_uni).
